    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.Combinatorics.Quiver.Prefunctor, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Prefunctors on paths and on vertices #

    Elementary facts about a prefunctor φ : Q ⥤q R which Prefunctor.mapPath and Prefunctor.comp leave unrecorded: pushing a path along φ preserves its length and maps its vertices along φ.obj, a prefunctor with a two-sided inverse is bijective on vertices, a pair of composable one-sided inverse pairs composes to a one-sided inverse pair, and a prefunctor that undoes another on vertices and arrows also undoes it on paths.

    Main results #

    • Prefunctor.length_mapPath: pushing a path along a prefunctor preserves its length.
    • Prefunctor.vertices_mapPath: the vertices of the pushed path are the images of the vertices of the original path.
    • Prefunctor.obj_bijective_of_comp_eq_id: mutually inverse prefunctors are bijective on vertices.
    • Prefunctor.comp_comp_comp_eq_id: composing two one-sided inverse pairs of prefunctors gives a one-sided inverse pair.
    • Prefunctor.cast_mapPath_mapPath: a prefunctor that undoes another on vertices and arrows undoes it on paths.

    References #

    The first three feed LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.PathAlgebra.mapAlgHom in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/PathAlgebra/Map.lean, whose uniform hypothesis is bijectivity on vertices, and the transport of the zigzag relations in TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Zigzag/Isomorphism.lean, which is stated in terms of path lengths. Prefunctor.cast_mapPath_mapPath gives the inverse laws for path transport along isomorphisms of bounded networks in TauCeti/Combinatorics/Network/Isomorphism.lean.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem Prefunctor.length_mapPath {Q : Type u} {R : Type u'} [Quiver Q] [Quiver R] (φ : Q ⥤q R) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) :
    (φ.mapPath p).length = p.length

    Pushing a path along a prefunctor preserves its length: the image path traverses the image of each arrow of the original, in order.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem Prefunctor.vertices_mapPath {Q : Type u} {R : Type u'} [Quiver Q] [Quiver R] (φ : Q ⥤q R) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) :
    (φ.mapPath p).vertices = List.map φ.obj p.vertices

    The vertices of a path pushed along a prefunctor are the images of its vertices, in order.

    theorem Prefunctor.obj_bijective_of_comp_eq_id {Q : Type u} {R : Type u'} [Quiver Q] [Quiver R] (φ : Q ⥤q R) (ψ : R ⥤q Q) (hφψ : φ ⋙q ψ = 𝟭q Q) (hψφ : ψ ⋙q φ = 𝟭q R) :
    Function.Bijective φ.obj

    Mutually inverse prefunctors are bijective on vertices.

    source
    theorem Prefunctor.comp_comp_comp_eq_id {Q : Type u} {R : Type u'} {S : Type u''} [Quiver Q] [Quiver R] [Quiver S] (φ : Q ⥤q R) (ψ : R ⥤q Q) (φ' : R ⥤q S) (ψ' : S ⥤q R) (hφψ : φ ⋙q ψ = 𝟭q Q) (hφψ' : φ' ⋙q ψ' = 𝟭q R) :
    φ ⋙q φ' ⋙q (ψ' ⋙q ψ) = 𝟭q Q

    One-sided inverse pairs of prefunctors compose: if ψ is a right inverse of φ and ψ' one of φ', then ψ' ⋙q ψ is a right inverse of φ ⋙q φ'. Applying this to a mutually inverse pair in each order gives both inverse laws for the composite pair.

    theorem Prefunctor.cast_mapPath_mapPath {Q : Type u} {R : Type u'} [Quiver Q] [Quiver R] (φ : Q ⥤q R) (ψ : R ⥤q Q) (hobj : ∀ (a : Q), ψ.obj (φ.obj a) = a) (hmap : ∀ {a b : Q} (e : a ⟶ b), Quiver.Hom.cast ⋯ ⋯ (ψ.map (φ.map e)) = e) {a b : Q} (p : Quiver.Path a b) :
    Quiver.Path.cast ⋯ ⋯ (ψ.mapPath (φ.mapPath p)) = p

    A prefunctor that undoes another on vertices and arrows undoes it on paths: pushing a path along φ and then ψ returns the original path once its endpoints are transported back.
